    Uniserial objects #

    The covering part of the magnitude proof uses modules over finite and locally bounded linear categories. This file packages uniseriality intrinsically as totality of the categorical subobject order, independently of any chosen category algebra.

    source
    def MagnitudeConjecture.IsUniserialObject {C : Type u} [CategoryTheory.Category.{v, u} C] (X : C) :
    Prop

    An object is uniserial when any two of its subobjects are comparable.

      theorem MagnitudeConjecture.IsUniserialObject.op {C : Type u} [CategoryTheory.Category.{v, u} C] {X : C} [CategoryTheory.Abelian C] (hX : IsUniserialObject X) :
      IsUniserialObject (Opposite.op X)

      Passing to the opposite category preserves uniseriality. The subobject-order correspondence reverses order, which does not affect totality.
